hero.title: Play Go in Lublin
hero.subtitle: Free entry and open to everyone. You don't need to know anything or bring anything — just come.

homepage.meeting_text: Go is a game that brings people together. Join our meetings in Lublin — in a friendly atmosphere, with no pressure and a warm welcome for new players.
homepage.reassurance_1_text: We'll teach you the basics in 15 minutes — no experience needed.
homepage.reassurance_4_text: Kids, teens and adults are all welcome — we often play as whole families.

start.title: Start playing
start.intro: Step by step, here's what your first visit to the club looks like.
start.story_title: What happens when I come for the first time?
start.story_step_4: Someone from the club will explain the basics and find you a partner.
start.story_step_5: You'll play your first game on a small board — quick and enjoyable.
start.story_step_6: Stay as long as you like.
start.faq_q_1: Do I need to know the rules?
start.faq_a_1: No. We'll teach you the basics on the spot — most people started from zero.
start.faq_q_2: Do I need to bring anything?
start.faq_a_2: No, boards and stones are provided. Just come.
start.faq_a_4: Go is for everyone — kids, teens and adults are welcome. We often play as whole families.
start.faq_q_5: I'm coming alone — is that a problem?
start.faq_a_5: Not at all. Most people come alone and immediately find a partner to play.

oklubie.title: About the club
oklubie.intro: The Lublin Go Club has been active since 2001. We share the pleasure of playing and discovering how many possibilities lie on a board with black and white stones.
oklubie.second_paragraph: Three players in our club have reached 2 dan, a high level of skill. Every such journey begins with a first game. If you don't know Go yet, we're happy to show you the rules and play together.
oklubie.typical_title: What does a typical meeting look like?
oklubie.typical_text: We play casual games, teach beginners and review games. Meetings are open and free — kids, teens and adults are all welcome. We learn and have fun together, often as whole families.

rules.title: Rules of the game
rules.intro: Learn the basics in a few minutes. The rules are simple — only the strategy is hard.
rules.step_1_body: Go is a board game for two players. The standard board has 19×19 lines, but beginners usually play on smaller ones: 9×9 or 13×13. Players take turns placing black and white stones on the intersections of the lines. Black always moves first.
rules.step_2_body: Placed stones cannot be moved. You capture an opponent's stone by taking away all of its liberties — the empty points connected to the stone by a straight line. Stones of the same colour standing next to each other form a group and share liberties. A single stone in the middle of the board has 4 liberties, but in the corner only 2.
rules.step_2_alt: Diagram showing the liberties of single stones and groups.
rules.step_3_body: When a stone or group has only one liberty left, we say it is in atari. It can be saved by placing a stone on the last liberty. If the opponent does this instead, the stone or group dies and is removed from the board.
rules.step_3_alt: Diagram showing an atari situation and the capture of a stone.
rules.step_4_body: The goal of the game is to surround territory — each empty point counts as one point. Whoever surrounds more empty points wins. The diagram shows the end of a 9×9 game: Black has taken the right side and part of the top, White the middle and the left side. The stones marked with squares are dead — they have not been captured, but they have no chance to survive and are removed from the board at the end.
rules.step_4_alt: Diagram of a game's ending with marked territories and dead stones.
rules.step_5_body: Some situations could lead to endless capture — this is called ko ("eternity"). After White captures a stone by playing at A, Black cannot immediately answer at B, because the board would return to its previous state. First they must play somewhere else, and only on a later move return to B.
rules.step_5_alt: Diagram showing a ko situation and points A and B.
rules.step_6_body: Points where the opponent cannot play, because they would have no liberty there, are called eyes. A group with at least two eyes is immortal — the opponent cannot take two points at once, so they cannot capture it. A group with one eye can be captured. The black group at the bottom of the diagram has two eyes, so it is safe.
rules.step_6_alt: Diagram showing a group with two eyes that cannot be captured.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This site belongs to Lubelski Klub Go. Below we explain what data we process and how we handle the image of people in photos.
privacy.data_body: We do not collect personal data from regular visitors — we use no cookies, no analytics tools and no contact form. Club administrators sign in via Google (through Supabase Auth); for that purpose their Google account data (name and email address) is processed, stored by the service providers according to their privacy policies. Published posts and photos are stored in Supabase.
privacy.photos_body: We publish photos from meetings and events only with the consent of the people visible in them. When in doubt, we default to group shots, hands or boards where no faces are visible.
privacy.minors_body: We publish photos of minors only with the explicit consent of a parent or legal guardian.
privacy.withdrawal_body: Anyone can withdraw their consent at any time and ask for their photo to be removed — write to us through the channels in the website footer and we will remove it promptly.
privacy.contact_body: For matters concerning personal data, please contact us via Facebook or Discord (links in the website footer).
